judgment.rationale: The Power Display maintainer confirmed the stale slider is an intentional tradeoff because periodic DDC/CI reads can take hundreds or thousands of milliseconds; this is expected behavior rather than an unowned defect.
evidence: The report covers PowerToys v0.100.1, installed via PowerToys auto-update, affecting Power Display.

Reported reproduction: After changing the brightness of a display with Power Display, the slider stays at the set level. Both internal and external displays usually have their own built-in methods to change brightness. So, after changing brightness using this built-in method and then activating Power Display, the brightness slider of Power Display doesn't correspond to the new brightness level—that was changed without using Power Display.…

Reported result: The brightness slider in the Power Display utility shows the brightness level set the last time the utility was used to change brightness, even when the brightness after that was changed without using the utility. Hence, the utility slider shows the wrong setting/number for the brightness level.

Expected result: If display brightness was changed without using the Power Display utility, the utility should display the correct brightness level—that is currently used by the display—on the slider when activated. PowerToysReport 2026-06-26-10-50-42.zip
